summary: the singleton's two teardown calls discard `teardownWorktreeInstance`'s answer, so a worktree that survived removal is named on no channel while the wave names its own
acceptance: Neither singleton teardown call discards the boolean: a worktree that survived removal reaches the operator's channel from the singleton leg as it already does from the wave's slot tail. The sentence gains no third copy — `grep -rn 'survived removal (fallback exhausted)' src/` names exactly one site, which the wave leg, the startup sweep and the singleton all reach, each supplying its own subject. Behavior-free on every path that removes cleanly: `pnpm tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm test` green, and the two existing warnings are byte-identical to what they emit today.
tests: a singleton whose worktree survives removal names the surviving path
a singleton whose setupWorktree hook failed names a worktree its teardown could not remove
notes: Verified on this tip: `src/worktrees.ts:692` swallows `removeWorktree`'s throw under the comment "Caller records the surviving path" and answers false. The wave records it (`src/waveTick.ts:516`) and warns at `:722`; the startup sweep warns at `src/worktrees.ts:939`. `src/singletonTick.ts` has no `surviving`/`cleaned` at all. The two warnings differ only in their subject — `${phase.name}` against `startup sweep`.
